slides.texte_overlay:
Stoic lessons that make
modern life easier
Focus only on what you control. Your effort, your words, your reactions. Traffic, other people's moods and the weather are not your job.
Expect obstacles. The Stoics imagined problems before they happened. When the train is late or plans fail, you're calm because you saw it coming.
Judge less, understand more. People act from their own fears and habits. Seeing that makes it much easier to stay patient.
Remember that everything passes. Good days and bad days both end. This thought keeps you humble in success and strong in hard times.
Read a little philosophy every day. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and old ideas help me with very modern problems.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Old ideas help me with very modern problems.

slides.texte_overlay: Live simply. You need less than you think. Fewer things to protect means fewer worries and more freedom. Own less, worry less.
Use the obstacle. A setback is a chance to practise patience, courage or creativity. Every problem trains something useful in you.
